prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale ground excludes spacecraft/launch/external-processing. Mission Control Center(Bluebell:local-voice-only) routes User Services Portal requests/constraints to Mission Planning System(Cedar), producing screened schedules/command preparation package; controls routine-command authority/elevated-access approved-role/time-limit. Ground Network Manager(Juniper:standing-rosters) confirms maintenance; triages antenna/link/site anomalies. Stations: North S-Band Antenna;South S-Band Antenna;Kiruna X-Band Antenna;Svalbard X-Band Antenna. Command Validation Gateway(Osprey) independently validates stacks; planning/release segregated; Mission Control Center/Spacecraft Operations Team concur before uplink. Faults preserve command-state/block discretionary commands/require specialist reconfiguration-review. Spacecraft Operations Team receives maneuver recommendation package/Antenna Deicing Notice; uses Pass Replay Packet for anomaly-reconstruction verification; leads spacecraft-safety triage. Orbit Determination Engine produces qualified orbital solution/Doppler Residual Report/Laser Retroreflector Window; Mission Planning System enforces approved window interval. Flight Dynamics Team screens maneuvers/conjunctions; produces Ephemeris Delta Note; assesses degraded orbit/timing. Flight Dynamics Facility(Mistral:legacy-shift-logs) supplies Star Tracker Mask File/controlled ephemerides/events; archive-queue orbit-quality notification precedes catalogue-validity update. Gateway mask acceptance requires baseline-matched integrity/configuration/operator-approval. Network Control System uses accepted-ephemeris pointing/Security Exception Ticket restrictions; enforces approved routes/logs changes. Telemetry Ingest Service validates inputs/preserves immutable session-tagged raw staging/supplies metadata/replay. Payload Processing Facility(Forgehouse:consoles/shift-logs) coordinates Primary Processing Cluster; eligible Backup Processing Cluster overflow uses identical image/rules. Lantern unresolved; preserves validated routing. Levels:0 ordered/deframed/times-preserved;1A detectors/context;1B radiometric; retain build/calibration/ancillary provenance. Payload Calibration Team approves/tests baselines/requests systematic-defect reprocessing/assesses integrity. Product Quality Service receives patch bundle/produces Product Hold List; mandatory failures block delivery; records scientific-update versus recovery reasons. Recovery:contractual-latency/acquisition-order unless mission-management override. Long Term Archive authoritatively retains raw/auxiliary/inputs/products/metadata; accepts processing/quality/checksum packages; stable identifiers/content-search separation; preserves replaced versions unless policy-authorized

New part:
S213: During triage, operators preserve volatile logs, current configuration state, operator console history, and relevant message identifiers before restarting services or changing routing.
S214: Evidence is stored in write-protected case storage with a chain of custody entry that identifies the collector, collection time, source system, and reason for capture.
S215: Forgehouse must quarantine suspect input and derived output when product lineage cannot be proven during an active anomaly investigation.
S216: Cedar suspends automatic schedule publication when a security or continuity anomaly could invalidate contact commitments or conflict with manual recovery actions.
S217: Continuity modes are declared by the Mission Control Center after consultation with the affected technical leads and are recorded with the operational objective, expected duration, and exit criteria.
S218: In monitor-only mode, command release is stopped, telemetry reception continues where safe, and engineering teams focus on stabilizing observability and protecting evidence.
S219: In essential-service mode, the ground segment prioritizes spacecraft safety contacts, time-critical telemetry capture, core orbit support, and protection of unrecoverable payload data.
S220: Primary Processing Cluster can pause nonessential production queues and reserve compute capacity for validated recovery runs from known-good inputs.
S221: If site degradation persists, processing work is transferred to Backup Processing Cluster only after input custody, software baseline, and operator authorization have been verified.
S222: Cross-site failover is coordinated through Ground Network Manager so that antenna allocation, network routing, firewall state, and contact schedules remain consistent.
S223: North S-Band Antenna, South S-Band Antenna, Kiruna X-Band Antenna, and Svalbard X-Band Antenna are placed in the recovery plan according to current availability and the spacecraft contact priority.
S224: Long Term Archive remains the custody reference during degraded operations, and any delayed ingest or publication is reconciled before normal service status is restored.
S225: User Services Portal communicates confirmed service impacts in operational terms and avoids publishing speculative root cause information before the incident lead approves release.
S226: Recovery is accepted only when command authority is verified, telemetry and product flows are reconciled, security monitoring has returned to the approved baseline, and responsible teams have signed the incident record.
S227: Routine mission service begins only after the operational readiness review confirms that ground procedures, staffing rosters, monitoring views, and escalation paths are under configuration control.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
